blocks.markdown: SSS benefits — objectives: compute the monthly pension (Sec. 12) from the AMSC, state each benefit's qualifier and amount (Secs. 12-A through 14-B), apply the Aguas beneficiary test and the Ortega disability doctrine, and track the current overlays (RA 11210 maternity, Circular 2023-009 funeral).

This lesson follows syllabus item II.2 in order: monthly pension (Sec. 12), dependents' pension (Sec. 12-A), retirement (Sec. 12-B), death (Sec. 13), permanent disability (Sec. 13-A), funeral (Sec. 13-B), sickness (Sec. 14), maternity (Sec. 14-A), and unemployment (Sec. 14-B). Master the numbers ladder first — 120-36-36 for pensions, 3-in-12 for sickness/maternity, 36 (12-in-18) for unemployment — then attach each benefit's conditions to it.

Three defined terms carry the whole benefits topic. The **AMSC** (Sec. 8(m)) is the pension base: the higher of (last-60-MSCs ÷ 60) or (all MSCs ÷ contributions paid). **Dependents** (Sec. 8(e)) are the legal spouse entitled to support, each qualifying child, and a regularly supported parent. **Beneficiaries** (Sec. 8(k)) stack into primary (dependent spouse until remarriage + dependent children), secondary (dependent parents), and designated secondary — with illegitimate children at 50% of a legitimate child's share when legitimate children concur, 100% when they do not.

Compute the AMSC both ways and take the **higher** result — that single instruction is the most testable sentence in Sec. 8(m). Because every pension formula is a percentage of AMSC, a member's lifetime MSC choices (including voluntary-continuation MSCs) directly set the pension base. Practical tip: low declared MSCs today mean a low AMSC tomorrow.

Secs. 8(e) and 8(k) work as a pair: (e) defines who counts as a dependent, (k) ranks them as beneficiaries. Three exam rules fall out: the spouse's status ends on **remarriage**; **illegitimate children share at 50%** beside legitimate children and 100% without them; and only **legally adopted** children count — informal adoptees are out (Aguas). Keep beneficiary designations updated: the designated secondary only inherits when no primary or secondary beneficiary exists.

Sec. 12's pension is the highest of: (1) P300 + 20% of AMSC + 2% of AMSC per credited year of service beyond 10; (2) 40% of AMSC; or (3) P1,000 — with minimums of P1,200 (10+ CYS) and P2,400 (20+ CYS), the P1,000 additional allowance (since January 2017), and a **60-month aggregate guarantee** that survivor provisions repeatedly invoke. Example: AMSC P15,000 with 25 CYS → formula (1) = 300 + 3,000 + 4,500 = **P7,800** vs. formula (2) P6,000 vs. P1,000 → pension P7,800 before the allowance. Peso figures are as stated in RA 11199 — confirm current pension amounts with SSS before relying on them.

Sec. 12-A adds **10% of the monthly pension (minimum P250)** per dependent child to every retirement, death, or permanent-total-disability pension. Caps: conceived on or before the contingency date, **maximum five children**, youngest first, no substitution, legitimate children preferred. Children conceived after the contingency are excluded — the contingency date freezes the dependent count.

Sec. 12-B opens two retirement doors with **120 contributions**: optional at **60 with separation** (or cessation of self-employment), mandatory at **65** (no separation needed). The prize is a lifetime monthly pension, with an option to take the **first 18 months as a discounted lump sum**. At 60 without 120, only a lump sum of total contributions — and the member must stop paying. Reemployment before 65 **suspends** the pension and restarts coverage; death passes the pension to primaries as of the retirement date (or the 60-month balance as a lump sum to secondaries); late retirees get the higher of earliest-possible or actual computation.

Sec. 13 turns on contribution count plus the beneficiary ladder. With **36+ contributions**: primaries draw the monthly pension; with no primaries, secondaries get **36 × monthly pension** as a lump sum. Below 36: whoever qualifies gets **(pension × contributions) or 12 × pension, whichever is higher**. Claims processors count first, then apply the Sec. 8(k) ladder through the Aguas lens (spouse must prove dependency; informal adoptees excluded).

Sec. 13-A mirrors Sec. 13's 36/12× structure for **permanent total disability**: 36+ contributions → monthly pension (+ dependents' pension); below → lump sum of pension × contributions or 12×, higher. The five deemed-PTD cases (both eyes, two limbs, two-limb paralysis, brain injury causing incurable imbecility/insanity, SSS-approved cases) are worth memorizing. **Permanent partial** disability uses the statutory schedule (arm 50, leg 46, hand 39, sight of one eye 25, down to little finger 3 months of pension); degrees (months ÷ 75, rounded up) aggregate only for deteriorating related disabilities to 100%, which converts to PTD. Under-12-month awards pay lump sum; partial-pension months count as paid contributions toward later claims; the pension suspends on reemployment, recovery, or skipping the annual exam — and Ortega confirms SSS medical findings control under substantial evidence.

Sec. 13-B's statutory P12,000 funeral grant is paid on any member's death, including PTD pensioners and retirees. **Current rule** (SSS Circular No. 2023-009, effective 20 October 2023): **variable P20,000–P60,000** where the member paid at least 36 contributions, **fixed P12,000** for 1–35 contributions — paid to whoever proves the funeral expense, separate from and additional to Sec. 13 death benefits. A question asking the 'current' funeral amount wants the circular figures, not the bare statute.

blocks.markdown: Sec. 14 pays **90% of ADSC per day** of compensable confinement (>3 days) on **3 contributions in the last 12 months**, capped at **120 days/year** (no carryover) and **240 days** per confinement. The notice chain decides most cases: employee → employer within **5 days**, unless hospital confinement or on-premises sickness/injury; unemployed/SE → SSS directly within 5 days (hospital excepted); late notice backdates the start to 5 days before notification. The employer advances every payday (after company sick leaves exhaust) and recovers **100%** — but only with timely SSS notice, else reimbursement starts 10 days before SSS notification; an employer that was duly notified yet fails to file **cannot recover its advances**. Claims prescribe in 1 year; delayed SSS reimbursement earns **1% simple interest/month** after a one-month grace.

Sec. 14-A as enacted (100% ADSC × 60 days, 78 caesarian, first 4 deliveries) survives only in its mechanics: the **3-contribution qualifier**, 100%-of-ADSC rate, **30-day employer advance**, 100% reimbursement, sickness-bar for the same period, and employer damages for unremitted contributions or missing notice. **Current rule** (RA 11210, effective 11 March 2019): **105 days** live birth (any mode), **60 days** miscarriage/ETP including stillbirth, **120 days** for solo parents — **every instance** regardless of frequency, with up to **7 days allocable** to the father or an alternate caregiver. Claims may be filed within 10 years of delivery.

Sec. 14-B pays **50% of AMSC monthly for up to 2 months** to members not over 60 with **36 contributions including 12 in the last 18 months** — once every 3 years, for **involuntary separation only** (authorized causes, never resignation or just-cause dismissal). Current procedure: claim within 1 year of separation, then secure DOLE's electronic Certification of Involuntary Separation within 30 days of the online SSS filing. The concurrence proviso is general doctrine: **concurring contingencies pay only the highest benefit**.

blocks.markdown: For payroll and compliance officers, three benefits run through the employer. **Sickness**: advance every payday after company sick leaves exhaust, notify SSS within 5 days of the employee's notice, file for 100% reimbursement — miss the notice and the advance becomes company cost. **Maternity**: advance the full computed benefit within 30 days of the leave application, transmit the pregnancy notice, claim 100% reimbursement — unremitted contributions or missing notice convert into employer damages equal to the whole benefit. **Unemployment**: issue separation documentation promptly so the worker can secure DOLE certification within 30 days of filing. Retirement, death, disability, and funeral bypass payroll — but all of them depend on contributions having been remitted on time.

**Trap**: '60/78 days' and 'first four deliveries' are repealed markers — current maternity is 105/60/120, every instance (RA 11210, 11 Mar 2019). **Trap**: the bare-statute P12,000 funeral is current ONLY for 1–35 contributions; 36+ draws P20,000–P60,000 (Circular 2023-009). **Trap**: illegitimate children share at 50% beside legitimate children — but take 100% without them. **Trap**: a separated, self-supporting legal spouse fails the Aguas dependency test.

**Exam memory set**: 120-36-36 / 3-3 / 36(12-in-18); pension = highest of 3 formulas + 60-month guarantee; dependents' pension 10%/P250 × max 5; AMSC = higher of 2 computations; 18-month retirement advance; 5-day sickness notices; 2-month/3-year unemployment limits; highest-benefit-only on concurrence.

Self-check: (1) A member with 30 contributions dies survived by a dependent spouse — pension or lump sum, and how much? (2) A worker is confined at home (not a hospital) for 6 days and notifies her employer on day 8 — when is her confinement deemed to have started? (3) A solo parent gives live birth in 2024 with 5 posted contributions — how many days of maternity benefit, and at what rate?

Takeaways: pensions run on the AMSC through the highest-of-three formula with a 60-month guarantee; qualifiers ladder at 120-36-36, 3-in-12, and 36 (12-in-18); beneficiaries stack primary-secondary-designated with Aguas guarding the spouse's gate; disability is adjudicated on SSS medical findings (Ortega), not Labor Code theory; and two current overlays must always be cited — RA 11210 for maternity and Circular 2023-009 for funeral.
